name: bgpq3
desc: BGP filtering automation for Cisco, Juniper, BIRD and OpenBGPD routers
why: Generates router prefix filters from IRR data, opening a window onto how internet routing policy is actually written, though it is mostly automation.

brief.what_it_is: bgpq3 is a command-line tool that generates BGP prefix filter lists for routers. You give it an AS number, such as AS20597, and a name for the list, and it prints a configuration snippet. The README's example uses the -J flag and produces a Juniper policy-options block with a prefix-list of the IPv4 prefixes for that AS. The homepage says it targets Cisco, Juniper, BIRD and OpenBGPD. The homepage does not name the data source, but the scout notes say it draws on IRR data.
brief.why_it_exists: The README's framing is that if you run BGP and want to automate filter generation for your routers, bgpq3 makes that easy. The author presents it as a way to stop maintaining prefix filters by hand.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage text does not explain the mechanism. From the example, you pass an AS number and a list name, and the tool outputs a router-ready prefix-list. The README does not say where the prefixes come from or how the tool fetches them.

commands_seen.context: Example invocation from the README. It generates a Juniper (-J) prefix-list named eltel for AS20597 and prints the policy-options block shown in the README. The prompt string is part of the README's illustration, not a required form.

brief.install_notes: The homepage lists a bgpq3-0.1.36.1-static1.i686.rpm package, which is a 32-bit static RPM. Source tarballs and man pages are linked for older versions. The README gives no build steps, dependencies, or first-run configuration. The brew description lists the executable as bgpq3.
brief.standout: The tool turns a single AS number into router-ready filter configuration for several different router platforms, which lets an operator avoid writing prefix lists by hand. The scout notes also point out that the output is a window onto how routing policy is written in practice.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage lists releases from 0.1.7 up to 0.1.36.1 and a 'CHANGES' section, but gives no dates and no last-commit information. The page's last-updated date is not shown, so I cannot confirm whether the project is active.
brief.caveats: The homepage is thin. It gives no install instructions beyond an RPM link, no data-source details, and no licence. It says 'Details and examples can be found in a man page below', but the man page content is not on the page, only links to tarballs. The 0.1.36.1 RPM is a 32-bit static i686 build, so it is not a general-purpose package. The README does not state what happens when a query fails or how it behaves on large AS sets.

Well, with BGPQ3 it's as easy as:
